problem_text:
A logistics manager is selecting cargo containers to load onto a transport vehicle. Available containers are:
* Container 1: volume 31 m³, revenue $210
* Container 2: volume 11 m³, revenue $59
* Container 3: volume 24 m³, revenue $91
* Container 4: volume 30 m³, revenue $59
* Container 5: volume 46 m³, revenue $87
* Container 6: volume 22 m³, revenue $29
* Container 7: volume 45 m³, revenue $68
* Container 8: volume 20 m³, revenue $169
* Container 9: volume 18 m³, revenue $99
* Container 10: volume 38 m³, revenue $116
* Container 11: volume 26 m³, revenue $251
* Container 12: volume 46 m³, revenue $295
* Container 13: volume 2 m³, revenue $147
* Container 14: volume 41 m³, revenue $214
* Container 15: volume 37 m³, revenue $67
* Container 16: volume 20 m³, revenue $199
* Container 17: volume 35 m³, revenue $292
* Container 18: volume 25 m³, revenue $157
* Container 19: volume 19 m³, revenue $50
* Container 20: volume 29 m³, revenue $125
* Container 21: volume 19 m³, revenue $252
* Container 22: volume 2 m³, revenue $132
* Container 23: volume 2 m³, revenue $66
* Container 24: volume 2 m³, revenue $181
* Container 25: volume 28 m³, revenue $83
* Container 26: volume 20 m³, revenue $30
* Container 27: volume 7 m³, revenue $60
* Container 28: volume 20 m³, revenue $249
* Container 29: volume 20 m³, revenue $81

The vehicle has a maximum cargo capacity of 479 m³. Select the container combination that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this volume limit. Each container must be either fully loaded or left behind.
